name: list_sprites
description: Discover open Aseprite documents, including when no sprite is open or bound. Returns {sprites:{items,total,offset,nextOffset?},activeSpriteId?,targetSpriteId?}. Items contain spriteId, filename, width, height, colorMode and frameCount. Does not activate or bind a document. Pagination defaults to offset 0 and limit 64 (maximum 256). Use switch_sprite to choose the editing target.

offset.description: Zero-based offset applied independently to each requested collection.

name: view_sprite
description: Render PNG preview sheets from a live, possibly unsaved Aseprite document. Returns sparse JSON (spriteId, target, optional revision, selectedFrames, clipped region, scale, layout and preview dimensions) plus PNG images; use inspect_sprite for structure. Discover IDs with list_sprites. Selection precedence: frames > tag > frame; frames are 1-based, explicit order/duplicates are retained, default is the captured target frame or frame 1 for another sprite. Layers are native IDs, groups include descendants, and isolation includes hidden layers without changing the document. Region coordinates are zero-based and clipped to the canvas. Grid spacing is in source pixels and is drawn only at scale >=4. Previews upscale/downscale and split into sheets <=2048 pixels; export_sprite creates source-resolution files. Only the bound editing target reports a revision; reading another sprite never changes the target. Missing documents return NO_OPEN_SPRITE; a missing explicit ID returns SPRITE_NOT_OPEN.

name: inspect_sprite
description: Query a live Aseprite document without rendering images or changing the editing target. Omitted/empty sections returns only a compact overview: spriteId, target, optional revision, filename, width, height, colorMode, captured frame, queryFrame, activeLayer when available, isModified, hasAssociatedFile and counts {layers,frames,tags,slices,cels,palette}. Counts describe the whole document; palette count uses the effective requested frame. Optional sections: layers, frames, tags, slices, cels, palette, selection. Collections return {items,total,offset,nextOffset?}; total counts the filtered collection before paging. Layers are flat native-ID records with parentId for children (roots omit it), without children arrays. The layers filter includes selected groups and descendants and applies to layers/cels. The overview frame remains the captured target frame (or frame 1 for a reference sprite). queryFrame always identifies the frame used for cels and the effective palette; it equals the requested frame, defaulting to the captured target frame or frame 1 for a reference sprite. Frames/tags/slices remain document-wide. Palette entries are {index,rgba}, zero-based index and #rrggbbaa; paletteFrame identifies the source frame of the palette effective at the requested frame. Selection is a single {x,y,width,height,empty} bounds object, unaffected by paging. Only the bound target reports revision. Missing documents return NO_OPEN_SPRITE; a missing explicit ID returns SPRITE_NOT_OPEN. Use list_sprites for IDs, view_sprite for PNGs, and inspect before proposing an edit.

offset.description: Zero-based offset applied independently to each requested collection.

name: read_pixels
description: Read exact pixel values of a small region (width*height must not exceed 4096). Without layer, returns the composited visible layers as #rrggbbaa hex strings. With layer (a layer id), returns that layer's cel pixels in sprite coordinates, transparent outside the cel: palette indices for INDEXED sprites, #vvaa for GRAY, #rrggbbaa for RGB. Optional spriteId and frame; no approval or revision required.

name: switch_sprite
description: Activate an open sprite by its list_sprites spriteId and bind it as the editing target. Returns only {spriteId,target:true,frame,activeLayer?,revision}. Later execute_lua edits use this target. Use inspect_sprite for structure or view_sprite for previews. No open document returns NO_OPEN_SPRITE; a missing ID while documents are open returns SPRITE_NOT_OPEN.

name: execute_lua
description: Propose short, terminating Lua for the captured sprite; the user must approve the complete code. Call inspect_sprite first and pass its revision as expectedRevision. The plugin rechecks the active sprite/frame/layer and revision, then owns one app.transaction and returns the result and new revision. For undoable pixels: local image = cel.image:clone(); image:drawPixel(x,y,pixel); cel.image = image. Raw drawPixel/pixels/bytes writes to an attached image do not create Undo and cannot roll back. Use native undoable APIs such as cel.image assignment, cel.position/opacity, layer.name/opacity/blendMode, and sprite:newLayer/newCel; layer visibility and locking are undoable inside this transaction. Only edit the captured sprite; do not save/open/close documents or cause external side effects. Environment: sprite, native app, Aseprite constructors/constants, basic Lua functions, math/string/table/utf8; no io/os/debug/package/require/dofile/loadfile/load. Native app is powerful: this is trusted approved automation, not a hostile-code sandbox. Errors roll back undoable edits only. Running Lua cannot be interrupted by Stop.

name: export_sprite
description: Encode native-resolution PNG frames, an animated GIF, or a PNG spritesheet from a live unsaved sprite without editing or saving the source. Selection matches view_sprite: spriteId, frames > tag > frame (default captured frame), layers and clipped region. Explicit frames retain order and duplicates; tags select their numeric range, not playback direction. scale is an integer pixel multiplier (default 1), with no preview resizing or grid. format png (default) or gif; output frames (default) or sheet (PNG only). Sheet columns defaults to ceil(sqrt(frame count)), padding is transparent spacing between cells (default 0), metadata=true adds JSON frame rectangles and durations in milliseconds. GIF uses native palette conversion, binary transparency and 10ms timing. Limits: 16,777,216 rendered/output pixels, each dimension <=16384. Returns paths in an owned temporary directory, not image payloads. Copy files to the requested destination using any authorized client file capability; never reconstruct image files from read_pixels. Files survive individual calls. Internal-chat files expire when switching chats/accounts or closing chat; MCP files expire when their external client disconnects or native control ends. No destination path is accepted. Inspect/export again if a historical path no longer exists.
